source: tools/horse_symbols.svg: silhouettes traced from Muybridge, The Horse in Motion (1878), in a 1280 x 816 box at the plate's pixel scale

rider.label: With rider
rider.what: Width / height of the bounding box of the traced silhouette, horse and rider together.

horse.label: Horse alone
horse.what: The same box with its top moved down to the horse's ear tip, the highest point of the outline in the front quarter of the box.

moment.what: Side ratio of the rectangle with the same second moments as the filled silhouette, rider included. It uses all of the area, so no single hoof or tail tip can move it.

min_rect.what: Minimum-area enclosing rectangle at any angle.
min_rect.why_not: Left out: its tilt swings from 0 to 57 degrees between frames, so it tracks the tilt more than the horse, and its SD is 2.0 times the plain box's.

sensitivity.what: Frames 1, 5, 9, 11 include a thin ground shadow under the planted hoof. Taking 20 pixels of height off each of them.

verdict: This horse, in this run, is not golden: with the rider its box averages 1.47 (95% CI [1.41, 1.54]), without the rider 1.80 (95% CI [1.71, 1.90]), and 1.618 falls between the two, inside neither interval.
caption: Bars are bootstrap 95% intervals for the mean (10,000 resamples). One-sample t-test against 1.618: p = 0.002 with the rider, p = 0.005 without. The 11 frames are one horse in one run, about 1/25 s apart, so they are not independent draws; read the intervals and p-values as rough. Frame 12, the horse at rest, is not in the means: 1.02 with the rider, 1.09 without. Of two other measures I checked, a second-moment rectangle also excludes 1.618; a tilted minimum box, whose angle swings with the horse's lean, does not.
notes: The traces include the rider, whose head is the top of the box in every frame.
The ear tip is the same point for any front cut from 22% to 27% of the box width, in all 12 frames.
Ground shadows in frames 1, 5, 9, 11: with 20 pixels trimmed the 95% CIs are [1.43, 1.55] with the rider and [1.74, 1.92] without; the verdict stands.
